inspection_outcome: False coefficient1 on auxiliary maximum boundary term; factor2 already proved suffices downstream; main theorems not refuted.

findings.title: The boundary term in the maximum-principle bound cannot have coefficient exactly one

anchors.location: Lemma 8.1, equations (8.16)-(8.18), especially the last paragraph of the proof

findings.printed_claim: Under (7.1)_1, (8.17) asserts ||u||_infty <= max{||u_*||_infty, c mu |B|^(1/n)}, where c depends on n,p,q,L_tilde, not on u_*.

counterexample.boundary_data: u_*(x)=M for a positive constant M.
hypothesis_checks: With H=|z|^2+1, F-H=|z+x|^2+1-|x|^2/2 >= 1/2 on B. Also 4H-F=2|z-x/2|^2+2-|x|^2 >= 1. Hence H<=F<=4H, which implies both (1.11)_2 and (7.1)_1 for the fixed constants above.

D_zz F=4I, so both the original and the strengthened lower and upper ellipticity assumptions hold. F is smooth. D_zF(x,z)=4z+2x, whose x-difference is 2|x-y|, within the stated alpha=1 coefficient bound with L=4.
The strict gap q/p=1<1+alpha/n holds. Thus the example is not caused by violating the paper's main growth assumptions.
u-u_*=(1-|x|^2)/4 belongs to W_0^{1,2}(B), and D_zF(x,Du)=0 identically.
For every admissible variation eta in W_0^{1,2}(B), F(u+eta,B)-F(u,B)=2 integral_B |D eta|^2. Therefore u is the unique minimizer in (8.15).
counterexample.contradiction: The actual essential supremum is M+1/4. For any proposed structural constant c in (8.17), choose M>c sqrt(pi). The displayed right-hand side then equals M, contradicting M+1/4<=M. The integrand, ellipticity constants, mu, and domain stay fixed as M varies.
counterexample.quantifier: This disproves existence of the claimed data-independent c, not just one numerical choice of c.

findings.alternative_readings: Reading (8.17) with an implicit multiplicative constant outside the maximum would avoid the counterexample, but the printed displayed inequality explicitly uses <= and places c only in the mu term. This distinction matters because adding constants to u is an exact invariance of the energy. No assumption D_zF(x,0)=0 is present; imposing it would be a new, unnecessary restriction.
findings.proof_diagnosis: The proof chooses kappa_infty >= ||u_*+||_infty and kappa_infty >= C mu, and obtains u_+ <= 2 kappa_infty. This proves 2 max{||u_*+||_infty,C mu} on the unit ball, not the printed maximum with coefficient one on the first entry.
complete_repair: Retain the factor 2: ||u||_infty <= 2 max{||u_*||_infty,C mu |B|^(1/n)}. The same modification applies to the two one-sided bounds.

In App(B_rho), ||u_tilde_epsilon||_infty <= (1+rho)||u||_infty+rho, rho<=1, and mu_delta<=2. The corrected estimate therefore still yields ||u_epsilon,delta||_infty <= C(||u||_infty+rho), exactly the permitted form of (8.12).

Consequently (8.13)-(8.14), the ordered weak limits, and the Theorem 2 bound retain the same stated type, with an enlarged structural constant. No change to the growth gap, integrability exponents, or limiting procedure is required.
findings.impact: The literal Lemma 8.1 bound is false. Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 are not refuted. The repair is fully local and preserves the only relevant downstream use.
findings.severity_reason: Minor is recommended because the supported issue is the overly precise constant in an auxiliary estimate, while the main proof needs and already states only its weaker constant-multiple form. The parent should apply the operative review contract to the final classification.

per_problem.verdict: Confirmed literal coefficient-one failure, complete local repair, no demonstrated main-theorem defect.
per_problem.hypotheses: B=B1 in R2, p=q=2, alpha=1, mu=1 and all structural constants four satisfy the actual non-strict p<=q and strict growth gap. No D_zF(x,0)=0 hypothesis is present. F=2|z+x/2|^2+2 is smooth. With H=|z|^2+1, F-H=|z+x|^2+1-|x|^2/2>=1/2 and 4H-F=2|z-x/2|^2+2-|x|^2>=1. These are stronger than H/2<=F<=8H required in (7.1)_1. Hessian 4I and x-flux difference 2|x-y| satisfy the additional structural assumptions as well.
per_problem.witness: For constant boundary M, u=M+(1-|x|^2)/4 has Du=-x/2 and zero trace difference. For every admissible variation eta, the exact energy increment is 2 integral |D eta|^2, proving uniqueness of the minimizer. Its essential supremum is M+1/4; for any proposed data-dependent c choose M>c sqrt(pi). All structural data remain fixed and the printed maximum equals M. Thus the quantifier is genuinely contradicted.
per_problem.source_and_counterevidence: The source image uses literal <= and places c only on the mu term. An implicit constant outside the whole maximum would avoid the counterexample but changes the printed claim. The actual iteration concludes u+<=2 kappa_infinity; it does not prove coefficient one.
per_problem.repair_and_impact: Choose kappa_infinity=max(boundary norm,C mu) and apply the same proof to -u, then rescale to obtain 2 max{boundary norm,C mu |B|^(1/n)}. At mu=0, (8.18) and Poincare give the original coefficient-one bound separately. The recovery bound (8.2), rho<=1 and mu_delta<=2 convert the repaired inequality into C(||u||_infinity+rho), exactly (8.12). The ordered delta-then-epsilon limits, (8.13)-(8.14) and all exponents are preserved. Minor is appropriate for this auxiliary overprecise constant.

per_problem.verdict: Reported scope and limitations are retained without expanding no-counterexample into full certification.
per_problem.reasoning: The report distinguishes scalar relaxed minimizers from arbitrary weak solutions and original-functional minimizers without vanishing Lavrentiev gap. It retains the strict ratio gap, mu>0/alpha<1/modulus requirements for optimal Schauder exponent, and the finite-exponent and p<=n conditions of Theorem 2. The displayed absorption t=(R/D)*n(R-1)/(2 beta) is <1 since D-R=1-n(R-1)>0 and 2 beta>alpha>n(R-1); n=3 has a strict spare margin, q=p gives t=0, and alpha=1 can be lowered to alpha'<1. These internal checks do not reprove the imported autonomous/Campanato/sharpness results. Historical finite computations corroborate general arguments, not universal validity by sampling.
